A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeSync and CodeSyncBench. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–E are readable, and corresponding methods, experiments, equations, and displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original CodeSyncBench and HumanEval evaluations, training-time measurements, and analyses of training sample counts and API types.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds legacy-reference CCT results and retrieval-based comparisons in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The signature-tracking, retrieval, AST localization, DeepSeek-V3 synthesis, and manual-verification pipeline remains unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices B–C. The new retrieval procedures are comparison baselines.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same six libraries, 220 APIs, CCT/ECT/MCQ tasks, and HumanEval. The legacy-reference control and retrieval comparisons extend evaluation within this existing coverage without introducing another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds RAG and SFT+RAG comparisons for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct in Table 6, introducing retrieval-based alternatives to parameter updating. It also removes the separate SFT comparator from Table 4 and Figure 2 while retaining SFT-LoRA. Table 3's nine-model comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds CodeBLEU for CCT/ECT and introduces legacy-reference and retrieval evaluation protocols. Table 4 drops HumanEval P@3/P@5 reporting, but Section 3.2 and Appendix D.2.2 still describe ten samples and P@5 ratios, leaving the underlying procedure unresolved. Table 6 also ambiguously labels its MCQ metric as CodeBLEU.

E4.justification: New Table 5 evaluates two Qwen models against legacy-code references to distinguish existing coding capability from adaptation to updated APIs. V2 also reports a 60% retrieval hit rate. The sample-count, API-type, and DeepSeek instruction-following analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Reported generation counts in Appendix D and the training-time error-bar presentation in Figure 5 remain unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds CodeBLEU scores and Tables 5–6, removes the separate SFT results, and replaces HumanEval scores and retention ratios throughout Table 4. For example, original Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct HumanEval P@1 changes from 25.49 to 65.24; unresolved protocol alignment prevents treating this as a comparable performance gain. Table 3 and the shared CCT/ECT/MCQ scores in Table 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Appendices B.3 and D.1 are unchanged. Table 5's upper-bound characterization is an empirical interpretation, with no new formal bound, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: an authentic API-update data engine and benchmark, and evidence that LLMs and existing updating methods struggle with API evolution. Revised scalability language does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets legacy-reference performance as an upper-bound estimate and attributes retrieval failures to similar API names and crowded code contexts, motivating combined retrieval and fine-tuning. Its claim that RAG beats SFT across all three tasks overstates Table 6, where MCQ scores are 34.26 versus 35.16. Section 2.2 also adds an unqualified correctness guarantee for filtered invocations.

D1.justification: V2 documents a vector database of target-library API signatures using text-embedding-3-large. The abstract changes the access pointer from Code-Sync, advertised for code and data, to naturalcc's codesync example, advertised for code only. Existing appendix prompts, hardware, and hyperparameters are retained; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for RAG, CodeBLEU, the embedding model, and several recent synthetic-data or multimodal studies. The LoRA reference disappears, leaving a question-mark citation in Appendix D.2.1. The principal positioning against synthetic API-update benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds a compact main-text Related Work section while retaining Appendix A, inserts the fine-grained Qwen analysis, and lightly revises the abstract, conclusion, and surrounding prose. Author, affiliation, publication, and acknowledgement information also changes. Most narrative and appendix text remains intact.

P2.justification: The central results display is substantially reorganized: Table 4 changes rows and metric columns, and Tables 5–6 are added. Figure 1 replaces the NumPy illustration with PyTorch while retaining the NumPy caption; Figure 2 removes SFT and changes its scales. Other figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: CodeBLEU, the legacy-reference control, and retrieval comparisons add useful validation opportunities. However, v2 replaces HumanEval results without reconciling its table with the retained protocol, overstates RAG's advantage over SFT, and still quotes a 31.59 CCT score after removing the SFT row supporting it. These reporting inconsistencies undermine interpretation of the additions, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
